patternDetails.description:
Specified quantity of both credit or debit card numbers and of associated phrases such as:-
* "csv"
* "Expiry Date"
* "Bankleitzahl"
* "American Express"
* "handelsbanken"

For a definition of credit card numbers that are detected please see the CCL description for "Credit card numbers [Universal]".
patternDetails.name: Credit card numbers - with phrases [Universal]

patternDetails.description:
Credit, debit, travel, store or membership card numbers using a common bank identification numbering system. Such as:-
* 16 digit card numbers (including MasterCard and VISA)
* American Express
* CUP (China Union Pay)
* Diners Club
* Itaú Unibanco
* JCB
* Maestro
* Royal Bank of Canada
* ScotiBank
* Verve
* magnetic track data containing card numbers

Card numbers must conform to the following:-
* Start with a "3", "4", "5" or "6" i.e. be a standard format ISO/IEC 7812 number with a Major Industry Identifier (MII) for 'Travel and entertainment', 'Banking and financial' or 'Merchandising and banking/financial'.
* If not 16 digits then start with a recognised Issuer Identification Number (IIN)
* Have an appropriate length for the card issuer
* Either be contiguous or have an appropriate digit grouping for the issuer
* Any digit groupings to be separated by a white space " ", dash "-" or dash variant
* Have a valid Luhn check digit
* Must not appear to be part of a larger digit sequence

NOTE: Card numbers used for other non-financial purposes but that use the same format as monetary cards will be detected as credit cards. This is because:- 
* These cards typically have high PII risk
* Loyalty cards (etc.) often do have an actual financial value or financial consequence
* Card issuers have been known to upgrade loyalty & travel cards to have a financial value
patternDetails.name: Credit card numbers [Universal]

patternDetails.description:
Card magnetic track 2 data according to the ISO/IEC 7813 specification.

This detection is included within the CCL "Credit card numbers [Global]". 
This CCL is provided as an optional level of granularity.

* Itaú Unibanco
* JCB
* Maestro
* Royal Bank of Canada
* ScotiBank
* Verve

* Start with a "3", "4", "5" or "6" i.e. be a standard format ISO/IEC 7812 number with a Major Industry Identifier (MII) for 'Travel and entertainment', 'Banking and financial' or 'Merchandising and banking/financial'.

patternDetails.description:
Specified quantity of both credit or debit card numbers and of associated phrases such as:-
* "csv"
* "Expiry Date"
* "Bankleitzahl"
* "American Express"
* "handelsbanken"

For a definition of credit card numbers that are detected please see the CCL description for "Credit card numbers [Universal]".
patternDetails.name: Credit card numbers - with phrases [Universal]

patternDetails.description:
Credit, debit, travel, store or membership card numbers using a common bank identification numbering system. Such as:-
* 16 digit card numbers (including MasterCard and VISA)
* American Express
* CUP (China Union Pay)
* Diners Club
* Itaú Unibanco
* JCB
* Maestro
* Royal Bank of Canada
* ScotiBank
* Verve
* magnetic track data containing card numbers

Card numbers must conform to the following:-
* Start with a "3", "4", "5" or "6" i.e. be a standard format ISO/IEC 7812 number with a Major Industry Identifier (MII) for 'Travel and entertainment', 'Banking and financial' or 'Merchandising and banking/financial'.
* If not 16 digits then start with a recognised Issuer Identification Number (IIN)
* Have an appropriate length for the card issuer
* Either be contiguous or have an appropriate digit grouping for the issuer
* Any digit groupings to be separated by a white space " ", dash "-" or dash variant
* Have a valid Luhn check digit
* Must not appear to be part of a larger digit sequence

NOTE: Card numbers used for other non-financial purposes but that use the same format as monetary cards will be detected as credit cards. This is because:- 
* These cards typically have high PII risk
* Loyalty cards (etc.) often do have an actual financial value or financial consequence
* Card issuers have been known to upgrade loyalty & travel cards to have a financial value
patternDetails.name: Credit card numbers [Universal]

patternDetails.description:
Card magnetic track 2 data according to the ISO/IEC 7813 specification.

This detection is included within the CCL "Credit card numbers [Global]". 
This CCL is provided as an optional level of granularity.
patternDetails.name: Credit card magnetic track 2 [Universal]

patternDetails.description:
Card magnetic track 1 data according to the ISO/IEC 7813 specification.

example.description:
Specified quantity of both credit or debit card numbers and of associated phrases such as:-
* "csv"
* "Expiry Date"
* "Bankleitzahl"
* "American Express"
* "handelsbanken"

For a definition of credit card numbers that are detected please see the CCL description for "Credit card numbers [Universal]".
example.name: Credit card numbers - with phrases [Universal]

example.description:
Credit, debit, travel, store or membership card numbers using a common bank identification numbering system. Such as:-
* 16 digit card numbers (including MasterCard and VISA)
* American Express
* CUP (China Union Pay)
* Diners Club
* Itaú Unibanco
* JCB
* Maestro
* Royal Bank of Canada
* ScotiBank
* Verve
* magnetic track data containing card numbers

Card numbers must conform to the following:-
* Start with a "3", "4", "5" or "6" i.e. be a standard format ISO/IEC 7812 number with a Major Industry Identifier (MII) for 'Travel and entertainment', 'Banking and financial' or 'Merchandising and banking/financial'.
* If not 16 digits then start with a recognised Issuer Identification Number (IIN)
* Have an appropriate length for the card issuer
* Either be contiguous or have an appropriate digit grouping for the issuer
* Any digit groupings to be separated by a white space " ", dash "-" or dash variant
* Have a valid Luhn check digit
* Must not appear to be part of a larger digit sequence

NOTE: Card numbers used for other non-financial purposes but that use the same format as monetary cards will be detected as credit cards. This is because:- 
* These cards typically have high PII risk
* Loyalty cards (etc.) often do have an actual financial value or financial consequence
* Card issuers have been known to upgrade loyalty & travel cards to have a financial value
example.name: Credit card numbers [Universal]

example.description:
Card magnetic track 2 data according to the ISO/IEC 7813 specification.

This detection is included within the CCL "Credit card numbers [Global]". 
This CCL is provided as an optional level of granularity.
example.name: Credit card magnetic track 2 [Universal]

example.description:
Card magnetic track 1 data according to the ISO/IEC 7813 specification.

This CCL is provided as an optional level of granularity.

schema.description: Contains data about a TLS certificate.

caMode.description: Mode of the certificate, either `CUSTOMER` or `AKAMAI`.

certificate.description: Value of the certificate in PEM format. ASCII, base64-encoded text starting with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` and ending with `-----END CERTIFICATE-----`.

certificateId.description: __Read-only__ A unique identifier for each certificate.

certificateRequest.description: Value for the certificate signing request (CSR). ASCII, base64-encoded text starting with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----` and ending with `-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----`.

createdBy.description: Name of the user who created this certificate.

createdDate.description: __Read-only__ ISO 8601 timestamp marking the certificate's creation.

expiredDate.description: __Read-only__ ISO 8601 timestamp marking the certificate's expiration.

issuedDate.description: __Read-only__ ISO 8601 timestamp marking the certificate's issue.

modifiedBy.description: Name of the user who most recently modified this certificate. If there haven't been any modifications, the value matches `createdBy`.

modifiedDate.description: __Read-only__ ISO 8601 timestamp marking this certificate's last modification. If there haven't been any modifications, the value matches `createdDate`.

status.description: __Read-only__ The certificate's deployment status. Either `CREATING`, `UPDATING`, `PENDING_DOWNLOAD`, `PENDING_DISTRIBUTION`, `PENDING_ACTIVATION`, `ACTIVATING`, `ACTIVATED`, `DEACTIVATING`, `DEACTIVATED`, `EXPIRED` or `INCOMPLETE`.

tags.description: TLS certificates allow you to establish a secure connection using the public key provided by your certificate authority (CA). You can specify an Akamai-issued certificate or a customer-provisioned certificate using a trusted third-party CA.
tags.name: Proxy certificates

tags.description: A policy is the rule set defining how SIA handles known or suspected DNS threats. You can assign a single policy to a location or multiple locations to a policy.
tags.name: Policies

tags.description: Built-in responses are automated messages displayed to end users indicating when their activity violates a policy.
tags.name: Policy built-in responses

tags.description: A set of default security threat categories for traffic that you can tailor to your organization's needs.
tags.name: Policy predefined security categories

tags.description: Data loss prevention (DLP) allows SIA to identify and block sensitive or confidential data uploaded from a corporate network and transmitted to the public Internet over an HTTP or HTTPS connection. A DLP dictionary contains the regular expression patterns that are used to find this information.
tags.name: DLP dictionaries

tags.description: The patterns used by a DLP dictionary to detect data loss.
tags.name: DLP dictionary patterns

tags.description: The regular expressions used by a DLP dictionary to detect data loss.
tags.name: DLP regexes

tags.description: After applying configuration changes to a site, policy, emergency list, or honeypot, you must deploy these changes to the SIA network to ensure the changes take effect. Changes typically deploy within 20-30 seconds.
tags.name: Deployment configuration

tags.description: A collection of the configuration changes made to an existing deployment.
tags.name: Deployment changes

tags.description: Forwards suspicious or malicious traffic to identify machines that are infected with malware, attempt to download malware, or make requests to command and control servers. They can also be used as an HTTP or DNS forwarder.
tags.name: Security connectors

tags.description: A custom response configuration allows you to direct suspicious traffic to a machine in your network where activity is recorded. Information about the user device that made the request is captured to discover the internal IP addresses of infected machines on the corporate network.
tags.name: Custom responses

tags.description: DNS VIPs are virtual IP addresses assigned to allow DNS to resolve the internal IP addresses to the hostnames.
tags.name: DNS VIPs

tags.description: A collection of application settings applied to each of your properties by default.
tags.name: Global settings

tags.description: A site is a named collection of public IP addresses that belong to a region or geographic area in your network, such as a CIDR block for an office branch or company headquarters. Use sites to compare the query's source IP with the IPs of configured sites. A site configuration must include the IP address of your Active Directory or other local DNS server used to communicate with SIA.
tags.name: Sites

tags.description: A sub-location is a named collection of public IP addresses within a defined site.
tags.name: Sub-locations

tags.description: When you sign up for SIA, you receive a configuration and associated ID. This configuration contains settings for all of your sites, such as locations, policies, and quick lists. You can configure network configurations, global settings, and add or remove connectors to your base SIA configuration.
tags.name: Configurations

tags.description: Acknowledgements contain SIA keys and the customer's original account configuration agreement.
tags.name: Acknowledgments

tags.description: Custom error pages allow the SIA admin to customize the error page displayed in a user's browser based on the configuration policy.
tags.name: Custom error pages

tags.description: These operations control the state of the configuration wizard process when the admin uses the wizard.
tags.name: Configuration wizard

tags.description: These operations control the bulk log export destination and schedule configurations.
tags.name: Bulk log export

tags.description: These operations allow the admin to assign policies based on users and groups.
tags.name: User and group-based policies

tags.description: Enables managing client configurations. The operations include the SIA clients and network configuration along with version management and ability to activate and deactivate on demand.
tags.name: Client configuration

tags.description: Tracks the client software versions deployed.
tags.name: Client versions

tags.description: Tracks the devices the SIA client is installed on.
tags.name: Client devices

tags.description: Configures network access settings for client devices.
tags.name: Client network configurations

tags.description: Configures notifications based on the location, threat category, or report type.
tags.name: Notifications

tags.description: A list is a set of domain and IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes that are known or suspected to be malicious for a specific category of threat.
tags.name: Lists

tags.description: By default, each policy is configured with Akamai security lists. These security lists contain domains and IP addresses identified by Akamai as threats in the category assigned to the list. Various network security resources are used to maintain and update these lists.
tags.name: Akamai built-in security lists

tags.description: A collection of known DNS hosts that have already been resolved by a domain.
tags.name: DNS cache

tags.description: Enables the SIA proxy to authorize connections from the on-premises proxy in a proxy chaining configuration. This setting adds the `Proxy-Authorization` header to these connections. The `Proxy-Authorization` header contains proxy credentials that authenticate the on-premises VPN. ETP validates these credentials before it allows connections from the on-premises VPN.
tags.name: VPN credentials

tags.description: Enables the SIA proxy to authorize connections from the on-premises proxy in a proxy chaining configuration. This setting adds the `Proxy-Authorization` header to these connections. The `Proxy-Authorization` header contains proxy credentials that authenticate the on-premises proxy. The SIA proxy validates these credentials before it allows connections from the on-premises proxy.
tags.name: Proxy credentials

tags.description: Tenant access is used by Managed Service Providers (MSP) to restrict and create separate access for individual customers. These same settings help you delegate access within an organization.
tags.name: Tenants
